title: Batch Environmental Covariate Extraction
text: collect_gee_data() primary function building environmental covariate tables. extracts values multiple GEE datasets one point locations across date range, returning single data.table ready modelling.

title: Batch Environmental Covariate Extraction
text: Key observations: modis_ndvi values repeat within 16-day composite window (image) era5_temp chirps_precip change daily srtm_elevation static — value replicated across dates
code: library(geefetch) gee_auth()  dt <- collect_gee_data(   lon = 138.6, lat = -34.9,   date_range = c("2024-01-01", "2024-03-31"),   datasets = c("modis_ndvi", "era5_temp", "chirps_precip", "srtm_elevation") )  print(dt) ##    point_id   lon   lat       date modis_ndvi era5_temp chirps_precip srtm_elevation ## 1:        1 138.6 -34.9 2024-01-01     0.3245     28.4          0.0             48 ## 2:        1 138.6 -34.9 2024-01-02     0.3245     30.1          0.2             48 ## 3:        1 138.6 -34.9 2024-01-03     0.3245     27.8          5.4             48 ## ...

title: Batch Environmental Covariate Extraction
text: Pass data.frame, matrix, sf object: can also pass sf POINT object — coordinates extracted automatically (transformed WGS84 needed):
code: sites <- data.frame(   lon = c(138.6, 149.1, 153.0),   lat = c(-34.9, -35.3, -27.5),   name = c("Adelaide", "Canberra", "Brisbane") )  dt <- collect_gee_data(   xy = sites,   date_range = c("2024-01-01", "2024-01-31"),   datasets = c("modis_ndvi", "era5_temp") )  # 3 locations x 31 dates = 93 rows nrow(dt) ## [1] 93 library(sf) pts_sf <- st_as_sf(sites, coords = c("lon", "lat"), crs = 4326) dt <- collect_gee_data(   xy = pts_sf,   date_range = c("2024-01-01", "2024-01-31"),   datasets = c("modis_ndvi", "era5_temp") )

title: Batch Environmental Covariate Extraction
text: dataset produces column named normalised ID: Aliases ("NDVI", "SRTM", etc.) resolved normalised IDs extraction, column names always consistent.

title: Batch Environmental Covariate Extraction
text: extraction fails particular dataset-date-location combination (e.g., satellite overpass, ocean point), value set NA warning emitted. Execution continues remaining datasets. Use na.rm = TRUE remove rows dataset columns NA:
code: dt <- collect_gee_data(   lon = 138.6, lat = -34.9,   date_range = c("2024-01-01", "2024-01-10"),   datasets = c("modis_ndvi", "era5_temp"),   na.rm = TRUE )

title: Batch Environmental Covariate Extraction
text: Use caching (enabled default). Repeated identical calls served disk milliseconds. Narrow date range. Time-series datasets require one API call per date per location. 365 days x 10 locations x 3 datasets = 10,950 calls. Use coarse-resolution datasets possible. ERA5 (11 km) MODIS (1 km) much faster extract Sentinel-2 (10 m). Combine static dynamic datasets. Static datasets (SRTM, SLGA, WorldClim, OpenLandMap) extracted per location, per date.

title: Batch Environmental Covariate Extraction
text: use nert TERN data geefetch GEE data, outputs directly compatible — return data.table coordinate/date structure:
code: library(nert) library(geefetch)  # TERN data (Australian soil moisture) tern_dt <- collect_tern_data(   lon = 138.6, lat = -34.9,   date_range = c("2024-01-01", "2024-01-31"),   datasets = "SMIPS" )  # GEE data (global climate) gee_dt <- collect_gee_data(   lon = 138.6, lat = -34.9,   date_range = c("2024-01-01", "2024-01-31"),   datasets = c("era5_temp", "chirps_precip") )  # Merge on date combined <- merge(tern_dt, gee_dt, by = "date")

text: add new GEE collection, need: GEE collection ID (find GEE Data Catalog) band name(s) extract spatial resolution (scale metres) temporal resolution ("daily", "8day", "16day", "monthly", "5day", "static")

title: Adding Custom GEE Datasets
code: gee_register_dataset(   name        = "gsw_occurrence",   collection  = "JRC/GSW1_4/GlobalSurfaceWater",   bands       = "occurrence",   scale       = 30L,   temporal    = "static",   description = "JRC Global Surface Water Occurrence 30m",   domain      = "Hydrology",   citation    = "Pekel et al. (2016). doi:10.1038/nature20584" ) ## v Registered custom dataset "gsw_occurrence". ## i Collection: "JRC/GSW1_4/GlobalSurfaceWater" ## i Available via read_gee("gsw_occurrence") and collect_gee_data().

title: Adding Custom GEE Datasets
code: gee_register_dataset(   name         = "modis_lc",   collection   = "MODIS/061/MCD12Q1",   bands        = "LC_Type1",   scale        = 500L,   temporal     = "static",   description  = "MODIS Land Cover Type 1 (IGBP) 500m",   domain       = "Land cover",   scale_factor = 1,   offset       = 0 )

title: Adding Custom GEE Datasets
text: registered, dataset works dispatcher batch extraction exactly like built-datasets:
code: # Single extraction water <- read_gee("gsw_occurrence",                    region = terra::ext(138, 140, -36, -34))  # Batch extraction dt <- collect_gee_data(   lon = c(138.6, 149.1),   lat = c(-34.9, -35.3),   date_range = c("2024-01-01", "2024-01-01"),   datasets = c("gsw_occurrence", "srtm_elevation") )

what: What the generic handler does (and doesn’t do)
title: Adding Custom GEE Datasets
text: Custom datasets use generic handler, : Loads collection Filters date (time-series datasets) Selects specified bands Applies scale_factor offset Extracts raster point values generic handler : Apply QA masking (qa_band processing) Compute derived indices (e.g., NDVI two bands) Handle complex multi-band logic need QA masking computed indices, consider opening GitHub issue request specialised handler.

title: Adding Custom GEE Datasets
text: Registered datasets persist current R session . use across sessions, add gee_register_dataset() call script .Rprofile.

title: Adding Custom GEE Datasets
text: dataset widely useful, consider contributing built-handler geefetch: Fork repository Add metadata .GEE_META R/handler_registry.R Add alias .GEE_ALIASES Write handler R/handlers.R (rely generic handler) Write convenience alias R/read_*.R Add tests tests/testthat/ Open pull request

title: Getting Started with geefetch
text: geefetch provides unified R interface extracting environmental covariates Google Earth Engine (GEE). Unlike GEE R packages, geefetch works without Python — uses GEE REST API directly via httr2 gargle. Key features: Python required — installs like normal R package 19+ built-datasets — vegetation, climate, soil, topography Single-function extraction — read_gee() dispatcher + convenience aliases Batch extraction — collect_gee_data() multi-location, multi-date, multi-dataset Automatic caching — repeated queries served disk User-extensible — register GEE collection gee_register_dataset()

title: Getting Started with geefetch
code: # From GitHub (development version, with vignettes) remotes::install_github("max578/geefetch", subdir = "geefetch",                         build_vignettes = TRUE)

title: Getting Started with geefetch
text: geefetch uses Google OAuth flow googlesheets4, googledrive, bigrquery via gargle package. non-interactive use (CI, HPC), use service account: first-time setup, gee_setup() provides step--step instructions.
code: library(geefetch)  # Interactive OAuth (opens browser) gee_auth()  # Check your connection gee_status() ## -- geefetch status -- ## v Authenticated: yes ## i Project: "earthengine-legacy" ## i Backend: REST API (httr2 + gargle) ## i Cache dir: '~/Library/Caches/.../geefetch' ## i Registered datasets: 19 gee_auth(path = "path/to/service-account.json")

title: Getting Started with geefetch
text: Extract MODIS NDVI region South Australia: result standard terra::SpatRaster — can use terra functions analysis, cropping, masking, export.
code: library(terra)  # Define a region of interest aoi <- ext(138, 140, -36, -34)  # Extract NDVI for a specific date ndvi <- read_modis_ndvi(date = "2024-06-15", region = aoi)  # Plot the result plot(ndvi, main = "MODIS NDVI — 15 June 2024")

title: Getting Started with geefetch
text: extract values specific coordinates, use terra::extract():
code: # Define some sites sites <- data.frame(   lon = c(138.6, 139.5, 140.2),   lat = c(-34.9, -35.5, -34.2) )  # Convert to spatial points pts <- vect(sites, geom = c("lon", "lat"), crs = "EPSG:4326")  # Extract NDVI at the sites values <- extract(ndvi, pts) print(values) ##   ID      NDVI ## 1  1 0.3245 ## 2  2 0.4512 ## 3  3 0.2891

title: Getting Started with geefetch
text: convenience functions (read_modis_ndvi(), read_era5(), etc.) thin wrappers around central read_gee() dispatcher. can use either form:
code: # These are equivalent: ndvi <- read_modis_ndvi(date = "2024-06-15", region = aoi) ndvi <- read_gee("MODIS_NDVI", date = "2024-06-15", region = aoi) ndvi <- read_gee("NDVI", date = "2024-06-15", region = aoi)  # alias

title: Getting Started with geefetch
code: gee_datasets() ##            dataset                          collection       domain resolution temporal ##  1:     modis_ndvi                  MODIS/061/MOD13A2   Vegetation     1000m    16day ##  2:      modis_lst                  MODIS/061/MOD11A2  Temperature     1000m     8day ##  3:      era5_temp       ECMWF/ERA5_LAND/DAILY_AGGR      Climate    11132m    daily ##  ... ## 19: openlandmap_ph  OpenLandMap/SOL/SOL_PH-H2O_...  Soil (Global)      250m   static

title: Getting Started with geefetch
text: geefetch automatically caches extraction results disk. Repeated identical queries served instantly:
code: # First call: hits GEE REST API (~2-5 seconds) elev <- read_srtm(region = aoi)  # Second call: served from disk cache (< 10 ms) elev <- read_srtm(region = aoi)  # Check cache size gee_status()  # Clear cache if needed gee_clear_cache()

title: Batch-extract GEE data at point locations — collect_gee_data
text: Extracts values multiple GEE datasets one point locations across date range. Returns single data.table::data.table one row per location-date combination one column per dataset. primary function building environmental covariate tables modelling.

title: Batch-extract GEE data at point locations — collect_gee_data
code: collect_gee_data(   lon = NULL,   lat = NULL,   xy = NULL,   date_range,   datasets = NULL,   depth = "0-5",   stat = "mean",   backend = c("rest", "rgee"),   cache = TRUE,   verbose = TRUE,   na.rm = FALSE )

title: Batch-extract GEE data at point locations — collect_gee_data
text: lon, lat Numeric vectors coordinates (WGS84). Ignored xy provided. xy data.frame, matrix, sf::sf object point locations. Must contain columns named lon/lat, x/y, longitude/latitude, sf POINT geometry. date_range length-2 character Date vector (c(start, end)), explicit vector dates. datasets Character vector dataset names aliases. Use gee_datasets() list available options. depth Character. SLGA soil datasets: depth layer(s). "0-5", "5-15", ..., "100-200", "". Default "0-5". stat Character. SLGA soil datasets: statistic. "mean", "ci_lower", "ci_upper". Default "mean". backend Character. "rest" (default) "rgee". cache Logical. Default TRUE. verbose Logical. Print progress table status messages? Default TRUE. na.rm Logical. Remove rows dataset columns NA? Default FALSE.

title: Batch-extract GEE data at point locations — collect_gee_data
text: data.table::data.table columns: date Date extraction lon, lat Coordinates (always included) point_id Integer point identifier  One column per requested dataset

title: Batch-extract GEE data at point locations — collect_gee_data
text: dataset produces column named normalised ID (e.g., modis_ndvi, era5_temp, srtm_elevation). Static datasets value replicated across dates.

title: Batch-extract GEE data at point locations — collect_gee_data
text: Failed extractions individual dataset-date combinations produce NA values warning. Execution continues remaining datasets. matches nert's resilient batch behaviour.

title: Batch-extract GEE data at point locations — collect_gee_data
code: if (FALSE) { # interactive() # Single location, multiple datasets dt <- collect_gee_data(   lon = 138.6, lat = -34.9,   date_range = c("2024-01-01", "2024-03-31"),   datasets = c("modis_ndvi", "era5_temp") )  # Multiple locations from a data.frame sites <- data.frame(lon = c(138.6, 149.1), lat = c(-34.9, -35.3)) dt <- collect_gee_data(   xy = sites,   date_range = c("2024-01-01", "2024-12-31"),   datasets = c("modis_ndvi", "era5_temp", "srtm_elevation") ) }

what: Authenticate with Google Earth Engine — gee_auth
title: Authenticate with Google Earth Engine — gee_auth
text: Authenticates GEE using Google OAuth via gargle::gargle package. authentication flow used googlesheets4, googledrive, bigrquery — Python required. non-interactive use (CI, servers), use service account JSON key file via gee_auth(path = "service-account.json").

title: Authenticate with Google Earth Engine — gee_auth
code: gee_auth(   email = gargle::gargle_oauth_email(),   path = NULL,   project = NULL,   scopes = .GEE_SCOPES,   cache = gargle::gargle_oauth_cache() )

title: Authenticate with Google Earth Engine — gee_auth
text: email Character. Google account email OAuth. Use NA force interactive account selection, "" suppress auto-selection. Default uses gargle::gargle_oauth_email(). path Character. Path service account JSON key file. Mutually exclusive email. project Character. Google Cloud project ID Earth Engine API enabled. Default "earthengine-legacy" (public project). Set project higher quotas. scopes Character. OAuth scopes. Default includes Earth Engine Cloud Platform scopes. cache Character. Directory OAuth token cache. Default: gargle::gargle_oauth_cache().

title: Authenticate with Google Earth Engine — gee_auth
text: Invisibly returns gargle token. Called side effects.

title: Authenticate with Google Earth Engine — gee_auth
text: automated pipelines (CI, HPC), create service account Google Cloud Console, enable Earth Engine API, download JSON key. authenticate :
code: gee_auth(path = "path/to/service-account.json")

title: Authenticate with Google Earth Engine — gee_auth
code: if (FALSE) { # interactive() # Interactive OAuth (opens browser) gee_auth()  # Specify account gee_auth(email = "me@gmail.com")  # Service account (CI / non-interactive) gee_auth(path = "path/to/service-account.json")  # Use your own GCP project for higher quotas gee_auth(email = "me@gmail.com", project = "my-gee-project") }

title: Register a custom GEE dataset — gee_register_dataset
code: gee_register_dataset(   name,   collection,   bands,   scale,   temporal,   description,   domain = "User-defined",   qa_band = NA_character_,   scale_factor = 1,   offset = 0,   citation = NA_character_ )

title: Register a custom GEE dataset — gee_register_dataset
text: name Character. Short, unique identifier dataset (e.g., "soilgrids_ocs"). normalised lowercase. collection Character. GEE ImageCollection ID (e.g., "projects/soilgrids-isric/ocs"). bands Character vector. Band name(s) extract. scale Integer. Native resolution metres. temporal Character. Temporal resolution: "daily", "8day", "16day", "monthly", "5day", "static". description Character. Human-readable dataset description. domain Character. Scientific domain (e.g., "Soil", "Vegetation"). Default "User-defined". qa_band Character. QA band name, NA none. Default NA_character_. scale_factor Numeric. Multiply raw values factor. Default 1. offset Numeric. Add values scaling. Default 0. citation Character. Citation string. Default NA_character_.

what: Read data from Google Earth Engine — read_gee
title: Read data from Google Earth Engine — read_gee
text: Central dispatcher GEE dataset reads. Accepts dataset identifier (name alias) delegates appropriate internal handler. use cases, prefer convenience functions (e.g., read_modis_ndvi(), read_era5()) provide named parameters dataset-specific documentation.

title: Read data from Google Earth Engine — read_gee
code: read_gee(   dataset_id,   ...,   backend = c("rest", "rgee"),   cache = TRUE,   max_tries = 3L,   initial_delay = 1 )

title: Read data from Google Earth Engine — read_gee
text: dataset_id Character. Dataset name alias. Use gee_datasets() list available datasets. ... Arguments passed dataset-specific handler. Common arguments include date, region, collection, depth. See convenience function documentation dataset-specific parameters. backend Character. "rest" (default) "rgee". REST backend requires Python; rgee backend supports advanced server-side computations. cache Logical. Use disk cache repeated queries? Default TRUE. max_tries Integer. Maximum retry attempts network failures. Default 3L. initial_delay Numeric. Initial delay seconds retry (doubles attempt). Default 1.

title: Read data from Google Earth Engine — read_gee
text: terra::rast() SpatRaster object.

title: Read data from Google Earth Engine — read_gee
text: Use gee_datasets() list available datasets metadata. Tier 1 — Specialised handlers (QA masking): modis_ndvi — MODIS Terra NDVI 16-day 1km modis_lst — MODIS Terra LST 8-day 1km era5_temp — ERA5-Land daily 2m temperature era5_precip — ERA5-Land daily precipitation chirps_precip — CHIRPS daily precipitation srtm_elevation — NASA SRTM 30m elevation (static) Tier 2 — Specialised handlers (soil, computed indices): slga_cly, slga_snd, slga_slt, slga_awc, slga_bdw, slga_phc, slga_nto — SLGA soil properties (Australia, static) sentinel2_ndvi — Sentinel-2 NDVI 10m (computed, cloud-masked) landsat_ndvi — Landsat 9 NDVI 30m (computed, cloud-masked) Tier 3 — Generic handler (global datasets): worldclim_bio — WorldClim V2 bioclimatic variables ~1km (static) openlandmap_soc — OpenLandMap soil organic carbon 250m (static) openlandmap_clay — OpenLandMap clay content 250m (static) openlandmap_ph — OpenLandMap soil pH 250m (static) User-registered: dataset added via gee_register_dataset() automatically dispatchable generic handler.

title: Read data from Google Earth Engine — read_gee
code: if (FALSE) { # interactive() # Using the dispatcher directly ndvi <- read_gee("MODIS_NDVI", date = "2024-06-15",                  region = terra::ext(138, 140, -36, -34))  # Aliases are case-insensitive elev <- read_gee("srtm", region = terra::ext(138, 140, -36, -34))  # Equivalent convenience function (preferred) ndvi <- read_modis_ndvi(date = "2024-06-15",                         region = terra::ext(138, 140, -36, -34)) }

text: Reads CSIRO Soil Landscape Grid Australia (SLGA) data Google Earth Engine. Supports 7 soil attributes, 6 depth layers, 3 statistics. static dataset (date required).

title: Read SLGA soil data from Google Earth Engine — read_slga
code: read_slga(   region,   collection = c("CLY", "SND", "SLT", "AWC", "BDW", "PHC", "NTO"),   depth = "0-5",   stat = c("mean", "ci_lower", "ci_upper"),   backend = c("rest", "rgee"),   cache = TRUE,   max_tries = 3L,   initial_delay = 1 )

title: Read SLGA soil data from Google Earth Engine — read_slga
text: region sf::sf, sf::st_sfc(), terra::ext() object defining spatial extent. Required. collection Character. Soil attribute extract. One : "CLY" — Clay content (percent) "SND" — Sand content (percent) "SLT" — Silt content (percent) "AWC" — Available water capacity (mm) "BDW" — Bulk density (g/cm3) "PHC" — pH (CaCl2) "NTO" — Total nitrogen (percent) Default "CLY". depth Character. Depth layer. One "0-5", "5-15", "15-30", "30-60", "60-100", "100-200". Default "0-5". stat Character. Statistic. "mean" (default), "ci_lower" (5th percentile), "ci_upper" (95th percentile). backend Character. "rest" (default) "rgee". cache Logical. Use disk cache? Default TRUE. max_tries Integer. Retry attempts. Default 3L. initial_delay Numeric. Initial retry delay seconds. Default 1.

title: Read SLGA soil data from Google Earth Engine — read_slga
text: terra::rast() SpatRaster. CRS: EPSG:4326. Values depend collection (e.g., percent clay, pH units PHC).
